solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Emin moved the goalposts of contemporary English art

indicators.note: letters that are moved get shifted about, so the word art is rearranged
goalposts stand at either end with the action between them, so the outside letters of contemporary flank the next piece

parts.note: its two outer letters, the goalposts, are C and Y

explanation.surface: A critic complains that one artist shifted the standards by which modern English art is judged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' turns ART into TRA; 'the goalposts of' takes C and Y, the ends of 'contemporary', and stands them either side of E for English.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracey Emin is the British artist famous for My Bed, so her surname clues her first name.

clue.text: TB virus could destroy so much

definitions.meaning: the standard abbreviation for a unit of data storage of a million million bytes, not the lung disease
a computer virus might wipe out this much stored data

explanation.surface: A warning that tuberculosis could cause enormous harm.
explanation.walkthrough: TB looks like tuberculosis, and 'virus' supports that, but both belong to computing: a data unit and malicious software.
explanation.definitionFit: Computer storage is measured in units, and TB is the usual shorthand for the one equal to a thousand gigabytes.

clue.text: Free six-pack? Shout of approval goes round very shortly

parts.note: a six-pack is a set of well-defined stomach muscles, informally abs

indicators.note: one piece goes round another, enclosing it

parts.note: ole is the Spanish cry of approval heard at bullfights
very cut short to its abbreviation V

explanation.surface: A beer offer: a free six-pack, greeted with a cheer that soon goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from blame or guilt is to pardon them, a verb sense matching the verb 'Free'.

clue.text: Topless representative welcomes French fashionista to lift and enhance

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so one piece contains another
a topless word loses its first letter

parts.note: a member, as in Member of Parliament, represents constituents

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting a word reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: Christian Dior was the French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A racy picture of a semi-naked politician hosting a French designer, with talk of lifting and enhancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' and 'enhance' suggest cosmetic surgery; in a down clue 'to lift' reads the designer upwards, giving ROID, and 'Topless' leaves EMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish a story is to add colourful details, so it means to enhance.

clue.text: Irrelevant work seen around very loud building site

indicators.note: one piece is seen placed around another, containing it

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

indicators.note: building puts things together in a new form, rearranging the word site

explanation.surface: Pointless labour carried out near a noisy construction site.
explanation.walkthrough: Off-piste is skiing away from the groomed runs; 'building' rearranges the site to ISTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Going off-piste in a conversation means straying from the topic, so it means beside the point.

clue.text: With mobile in the air, fellow and son around resort snapped war aircraft

parts.note: moving through the air means airborne, on the wing

indicators.note: the two letters sit around the next piece, enclosing it
something snapped is broken, so the word resort is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A holiday snap: a man and his son phoning from a plane photograph a resort and a warplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snapped' reads like taking a photo, but signals a break-up of the letters, ORTRES.
explanation.definitionFit: The B-17 bomber, nicknamed for its heavy defensive guns, was a famous Second World War aircraft.

clue.text: Wrinkly thing to continue during record doing the twist

indicators.note: one piece happens during another, so it sits inside it
twisting round turns the word to face the other way

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
to run is to continue, as a play runs for a year

explanation.surface: An elderly person keeps dancing the twist while a record plays.
explanation.walkthrough: The twist is a 1960s dance, but 'doing the twist' turns the record round to PE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried plum is shrivelled and lined, a wrinkled thing; also a jokey term for an old person.

clue.text: Scrap eggy dish that's old, replaced by Charlie

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out and another put in its place

parts.note: a souffle is a light baked dish of whipped egg whites
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cook throws out a stale egg dish and makes another for someone called Charlie.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a brief rough fight, a tussle or minor brawl.

clue.text: Musical sibling balanced short track

indicators.note: cut short, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: evenly matched or level means even
RLY is an abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A sibling in a musical family plays a short, well-balanced piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The Everly Brothers, Don and Phil, were an American close-harmony duo of the 1950s and 60s.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the two singing brothers carried this surname, so either is a musical sibling.

clue.text: Suitable man from wings to pour hot tea over porcelain, after Church

indicators.note: the tea and porcelain come after the church
in a down clue the tea sits over, above, the porcelain
the wings of a word are its two outside letters

parts.note: hot, as in fashionable, means in
CE is the Church of England
char is a British slang word for tea
Ming is fine Chinese porcelain from the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: Instructions for a tea party: pour from the side, hot tea over fine china, after church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suitable' here means fit to be a suitor: the ideal romantic hero of fairy tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of Cinderella is the ideal suitor, a pun on suitable as suitor-able.

clue.text: Bird lovers nurse a stray with unknown fruit

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold and care for, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: the RSPB is the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds, a UK bird charity
to err is to stray from the right path
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Animal lovers take in a stray bird along with some mystery fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A red soft berry from a bramble-like cane, used in jams and desserts.

clue.text: Lab equipment taken from workplace, but usually returned

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Kit removed from an office is normally given back.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'taken' in the definition, but 'taken from' signals the letters lie inside 'workplacE BUT Usually'; 'returned' reads EBUTU backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped glass tube is standard apparatus in a chemistry laboratory.

clue.text: Revolutionary party idiot — symbol of party?

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
a loon is a silly or crazy person

explanation.surface: A left-wing radical calls a fellow member a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a radical, but signals reading backwards, BAL. The question mark flags one example of a party symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflated rubber decorations are a typical emblem of a celebration or birthday do.

clue.text: Poor, unfed, requiring drug hostel ultimately?

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hungry addict looks for a hostel at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges UNFED with E to give NEEDFU; 'ultimately' adds L from 'hostel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic or formal adjective meaning necessary, as in 'do the needful', so lacking and wanting.

clue.text: Current pair of trailing curtains

parts.note: the first two letters of trailing are T and R
curtains is slang for the finish, as in 'it's curtains for him'

explanation.surface: Curtains dragging along the floor in a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtains' means death or the finish, not drapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A prevailing direction or fashion is the current one, as in current thinking.

clue.text: Compulsory object bound for church

indicators.note: to bound something is to form its boundary, enclosing it

parts.note: an end is an aim or object, as in means to an end
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An item tied up and headed for church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'heading for', but here END bounds FOR and CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imposed by authority is obligatory, made mandatory rather than chosen.

clue.text: Criminal group receive stolen goods and appropriate funds

parts.note: a ring is a gang of criminals, as in a drugs ring
to fence is to deal in stolen property

explanation.surface: A gang handles stolen goods and pockets the proceeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee money for one purpose, earmarking it and keeping it protected from other uses.

clue.text: Fan 'eld by that woman on hospital department

parts.note: held means had; dropping the H as the apostrophe does gives 'ad
her refers to a woman already mentioned
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A fan clutched in Cockney fashion by a woman on a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eld is held with the H dropped, Cockney style; held means had, so 'ad, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or supporter of a cause or person, a devotee like a fan.

clue.text: Choir regularly interrupts self-catering woman's baking day

indicators.note: a piece that interrupts others breaks in among them

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation in holiday listings for self-catering

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word

parts.note: her is the woman's, a possessive

explanation.surface: A singing group disturbs a lone woman cooking for herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives COR, the odd letters of the choir; 'baking day' is the weather, not cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A very hot sunny day is informally called this, as is a baking-hot one.

clue.text: It's a choice between sophisticated and Yankee coffee substitute

parts.note: chic means stylish and sophisticated
or offers a choice between alternatives
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A café menu choice between a smart option and an American coffee alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'choice between' sits literally between the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The roasted, ground root of this plant is used in place of coffee or to stretch it.

clue.text: Hill? Driver reversed Rover

indicators.note: reversed says the word is read backwards

parts.note: Damon Hill is the British racing driver, 1996 Formula One champion

explanation.surface: A Land Rover driver backs up a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover looks like the car, given 'Driver', but it means a wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is a wanderer, one who moves from place to place with no fixed home.

clue.text: Mile award for cross-country type?

parts.note: a grant is a sum of money awarded

explanation.surface: A prize for running the mile, given to a cross-country runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross-country type' suggests a runner, but means someone moving across national borders.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who moves from one country to another, crossing frontiers to settle elsewhere.

clue.text: Leaderless fat guards stole on QE2?

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, enclosing another piece
without its leader the word loses its first letter

parts.note: lard is pig fat
a boa is a long feathery scarf, a kind of stole

explanation.surface: A fat captain-less crew watches over a stolen item on the liner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' is the scarf, not theft; 'Leaderless' leaves ARD. QE2 is the Cunard liner Queen Elizabeth 2.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship like the QE2 is on board, the question mark flagging one example.

clue.text: Skin surgery might improve this minor celeb

definitions.meaning: a raised bubble of fluid under the skin, which might be lanced

explanation.surface: A cosmetic-surgery jibe at a fading celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as B-LISTER, someone on the B-list rather than the A-list of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin bubble raised by friction or burns; and a second-tier famous person off the B-list.

clue.text: Steps back to sunless UK, and gradually sees ___?

definitions.meaning: the steps of a Latin American ballroom dance

definitions.text: back to sunless UK, and gradually sees ___?
definitions.meaning: fill the blank with two words: a holidaymaker back home sees the bronzed skin fade

explanation.surface: A returning holidaymaker watches something fade in the grey British weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is filled by the answer split in two: TAN GO, the suntan going.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American dance for two, so its moves are the steps; the blank is a pun.

clue.text: Exile gets official uniform — fancy that!

parts.note: a ref, referee, is a match official
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet
gee is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A banished man gets a referee's kit, to general surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is someone forced from their homeland, as is one fleeing persecution.

clue.text: Plug Roger connects on deck

parts.note: a plug is an advertisement, an ad

indicators.note: Roger connects the two letters of on by sitting between them

parts.note: R stands for Roger, received, in radio talk

explanation.surface: A radio operator called Roger wires a plug on a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like a noun for a ship's floor, but it is the verb to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck out a room is to decorate it, to embellish it with ornaments.

clue.text: Indirectly suggest annuities should be distributed

indicators.note: letters that are distributed are spread around in a new order

explanation.surface: A hint that pension payouts should be shared out.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something unpleasant without stating it openly, an imply-by-innuendo verb.

clue.text: Brass controlling railway start to consider complaint

indicators.note: one piece controls another by holding it inside

parts.note: brass and dough are both slang for money

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Top brass in charge of the railways begin to look at a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' looks like senior officers but means money; 'complaint' is an ailment, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be a minor illness, and an unproductive throat irritation is one such ailment.

clue.text: Netball team training in court close to contest

indicators.note: one piece sits in another

parts.note: a see is a bishop's seat and court, as the Holy See is the papal court
PT is physical training

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A netball side practising in court near the end of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A netball side fields seven players, and a group of seven is a set of that size.
